To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

surgery for brain metastasis should be considered for the following indications: (1) to obtain histologic diagnosis, (2) to improve local tumor and overall control, (3) to improve quality of life, and (4) to prolong overall survival.

surgery for brain metastasis is indicated in the following situations: 1) in cases of symptomatic lesions; 2) to improve local control and to prolong survival in cases of single or oligo metastases; 3) for histological confirmation of diagnosis in cases of unknown primary tumors; 4) in cases of large lesions (>3 cm) or multiple lesions (>4) in order to reduce the risk of radiation necrosis; 5) to reduce the need for WBRT;
surgery for patients with brain metastases is indicated for histologic diagnosis, to improve local control and to prolong survival.
